name: Jawbox
label: Dischord
lede: The band that handed Atlantic a list of demands nobody expected them to meet, got every one, and ended up with a song on Beavis and Butt-Head and hate mail from home.

eras.title: A sink, a sewer, a television
eras.text: J. Robbins had been playing bass in Government Issue; now he wanted his own band, on guitar and singing. With Kim Coletta on bass and Adam Wade on drums, Jawbox came up fast in a D.C. scene that was trading hardcore speed for something knottier.

years.h: A trio with a name out of an old reference book
years.p: Robbins, Coletta and Wade pull the name from Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable, where a jawbox is a sink, a sewer, or slang for the television.

Jawbox play their first gig on a bill with Fugazi and [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]], two bands whose paths will keep crossing theirs. A self-titled demo EP circulates the same year, and the song Bullet Park lands on a Maximumrocknroll compilation.
The debut single comes out as a split between Dischord and DeSoto, the label run by Coletta that will house Jawbox's vinyl for the rest of their life.

eras.title: Two guitars, and a chair at the drum kit
eras.text: The Dischord years were short and loud. A second guitarist doubled the band's reach, a Chicago engineer gave them a heavier sound, and by the end of it the original drummer was gone.

years.p: Produced by [[Eli Janney|d727e531-da9c-4124-ac66-0f79fb884d45]] for under $2,000. Robbins later said you can hear exactly which records they were listening to. Grip is the one song from it they kept playing.

[[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]], Adam Wade's friend and roommate, joins on guitar and vocals around the Grippe release. The same year brings a split single with [[Jawbreaker|ec88cdc3-0517-4951-b5ef-7323e7316db0]] and a tour with [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]].
A Dischord single between the two albums, released in early 1992.

q: Jawbox sold like 40,000. The next step up really is Minor Threat and Fugazi.
years.p: Five days in Chicago with [[Iain Burgess|1572ff4f-9714-4d7e-804a-49b86a74a855]], who had recorded [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] and [[Naked Raygun|85d2e30c-92fd-4c7f-a2dc-f988a70e234d]], and who slept on Robbins' couch. Robbins said the sound really started to expand with Barbot in the band.
years.xp: Novelty and Grippe made Jawbox one of the label's bigger sellers. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], sizing up Dischord's catalog, put them just below the label's two giants.

years.p: Right after the Novelty tour, Wade quits and soon joins [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]]. [[Zach Barocas|0c8ab49f-f5d0-46b5-bee5-5aa496a70ece]], a friend already living in the band's building, takes the drums.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Wade had grown frustrated with what was going on inside the band before and during that tour: Robbins and [[Kim Coletta|f220e94d-883b-46ce-a459-9463cce7f55d]] had ended their relationship, Coletta and [[Bill Barbot|c0407a04-3b21-4274-9ed1-695fbc07b218]] had become a couple, and Robbins' behavior turned erratic. He left as soon as the tour was over.

Barocas settled things. Robbins said his arrival really changed the band.

eras.title: Impossible demands, all accepted
eras.text: Grunge had every major label shopping in punk basements, and Jawbox had offers from Epic, Mercury and Atlantic. They took one, left Dischord, and kept a surprising amount of control, which didn't stop the scene from treating it as a betrayal.

years.p: One last single on the home label, two songs pointing straight at the major-label album to come.

years.big: They asked for everything. Atlantic said yes.
q: We would be stupid not to do it.
years.p: The band sent over what they called a list of impossible demands: self-management, full creative control, vinyl on DeSoto. Atlantic agreed to all of it.
years.xp:
The list also covered the recording budget, merchandising and European licensing. Jawbox turned down a big advance and tour support, and asked only for studio money and enough to settle old bills. [[Mike Gitter|942763ba-3882-48b4-b0a4-513f53849530]], who knew them from the Boston hardcore scene, was their A&R man.

Home took it badly. One letter-writer, the band later recalled, said he hoped they died in a fiery van accident. Barocas later said the deal kept them together: he had already quit and applied to the University of Maryland.

years.h: For Your Own Special Sweetheart · Atlantic / DeSoto
years.p: Produced by [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]], of early [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] records. Seven weeks in the studio against the seven days they were used to. It peaks at No. 28 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and, per Wikipedia, sells roughly 50,000 copies.

The single goes into regular rotation on MTV's 120 Minutes, gets played in-studio there and on Late Night with Conan O'Brien, and turns up on Beavis and Butt-Head. The follow-up, Cooling Card, barely registers.
A year after leaving Dischord, Jawbox are the support act on a Stone Temple Pilots tour.

eras.title: Their best record, and a label that folded under it
eras.text: Jawbox made the album Robbins still calls their best, then watched the Atlantic imprint releasing it disappear. By 1997 the drummer was headed for film school and the band was done.

years.p: A shared live LP in Germany's Your Choice Live Series. They also cut sessions for John Peel.

years.h: First band on at the HFStival
years.p: Jawbox open the big D.C. radio festival, the hometown band on the day's earliest slot.

Produced by [[John Agnello|c7d979e9-3b10-43db-973b-7da55a8a33c7]]. Atlantic moves them to TAG, a new alternative imprint that folds soon after. A cover of [[Tori Amos|c0b2500e-0cef-4130-869d-732b23ed9df5]]' Cornflake Girl hides at the end. Wikipedia puts sales at around 40,000. Robbins said the record fizzled with the label but still calls it their best.
years.xp:
Desert Sea, Robbins' favorite on the album, came out of a jam. Mirrorful was the single.

TAG folded not long after the album came out. In early 1997 the band and Atlantic agreed to part ways.

years.p: The drummer heads to Hunter College in New York. [[Peter Moffett|09d1a7e7-51fd-4b48-b99b-5b6bcbc8865b]], ex-[[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]], steps in, but a planned European tour is scrapped.
years.xp:
It wasn't the first time he'd walked. Barocas had already quit once and applied to the University of Maryland, and said the Atlantic deal was what kept the band going. This time he went to Hunter College in New York to study film.

[[Peter Moffett|09d1a7e7-51fd-4b48-b99b-5b6bcbc8865b]], who had drummed in [[Government Issue|9b952ee8-d45d-4a26-8066-57849d871e06]] and Wool, took over, but the European dates were cancelled and the band broke up later that year. Moffett stayed with Robbins and Barbot in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.p: With the Atlantic deal over and the line-up changed again, the band formally breaks up.
With the band finished, the bassist and the second guitarist get married, Wikipedia reports.
years.xp: They had a son in 2001. According to Wikipedia, Coletta and Barbot divorced shortly after 2009. Both were back on stage together for the 2019 reunion, and Coletta kept running DeSoto.

eras.title: Scrapbooks and airplanes
eras.text: The odds and ends got collected, and Robbins and Barbot went straight into another band with Jawbox's last drummer. Robbins was also becoming one of the busiest producers in post-hardcore.

years.p: B-sides, outtakes, Peel Sessions, live tracks and covers, gathered on Coletta's label.

Robbins, Barbot and Moffett's new band starts releasing records on DeSoto. Robbins' producer credits pile up: [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]], [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]], [[Shiner|85e4c862-bafe-48a2-a7af-b87cc3d8a7f3]], later [[Against Me!|a66ebddc-ff04-46b8-820a-15c63e80dba1]] and [[Clutch|0cdb0359-5698-487d-9aae-a25fb4dcdc4d]].
Burning Airlines break up after the aftermath of September 11 derails their touring.

eras.title: One song on network TV
eras.text: Twelve years after the split, the Atlantic debut came back into print on the band's own terms, and Jawbox played exactly one show to celebrate it.

years.p: DeSoto and Dischord team up to reissue For Your Own Special Sweetheart, remastered by Bob Weston on CD and LP with new artwork.

years.cap: Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, December 8, 2009
years.h: The reunion is a TV spot
years.p: Jawbox play Savory on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, their first performance since 1997. 68 and FF=66 go online as extras. Then they go home.
years.xp:
The occasion was the DeSoto and Dischord reissue of For Your Own Special Sweetheart, back in print for the first time in years. Savory went out on the broadcast; 68 and FF=66 were posted online.

It was billed as a one-off, and it was. The next Jawbox show was almost ten years away.

eras.title: Back on the road, then done again
eras.text: This time it was a real reunion: tours, a live album, even new recordings. It ran six years, swapped one guitarist, and ended with a quiet confirmation in a newsletter.

years.h: First tour in more than twenty years
years.p: Jawbox announce a 12-date summer tour with the Robbins, Coletta, Barbot and Barocas line-up. A Chicago show at the Metro becomes Live at Metro Chicago 2019 on Arctic Rodeo.

Jawbox announce that Barbot is leaving, citing the long commute from his new home in Vermont. [[Brooks Harlan|f9cb849f-568b-4987-b9cc-96e0e5d7d790]], guitarist in [[War on Women|69c05e9a-883b-4570-9c3d-c4bfc896a488]] and a longtime Robbins collaborator, takes his place.
Self-released first, then put out by Arctic Rodeo, which also handles the Metro live album.
Best Friends Forever festival turns out to be the final show.
Robbins confirms to Kyle Ryan's Band Name Bureau newsletter that Jawbox is done for the foreseeable future. No reason given.
